headline: Jamaat leader's son stabbed in Kishoreganj
summary: Shahriar Zaman Rana was attacked by an unidentified assailant in the chest at Gachihatta Bazar.
details: Shahriar Zaman Rana, the elder son of Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mohammad Aktaruzzaman Ranjan, was stabbed in the chest at Gachihatta Bazar in Kishoreganj's Katiadi Upazila.
The attack occurred around 8pm on Wednesday. An unidentified assailant stabbed Rana in the right side of his chest before fleeing the scene.
Local residents immediately rushed him to the Katiadi Upazila Health Complex for emergency treatment. He was later transferred to Jahurul Islam Medical College Hospital in Bajitpur for further care.
Katiadi police chief Mohammad Rafiqul Islam stated that police were deployed to the area following the report.
The identity of the perpetrators and the motive behind the attack remain unclear at this stage, according to the police chief.
An investigation is currently underway to determine the motive and apprehend those responsible for the attack.

headline: 491mmcfd drop in gas supply as Summit LNG terminal shut for maintenance
summary: National grid supply fell to 2,079mmcfd, lower than Petrobangla's forecast, as the Moheshkhali terminal closes for repairs until Nov 7.
details: Gas supply across the country has fallen by 491 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) following the shutdown of the Summit LNG terminal in Moheshkhali for maintenance.
The maintenance work began at 8am on Wednesday and is scheduled to continue until 4pm on November 7.
While Petrobangla forecast a drop to 2,250mmcfd, the actual supply to the national grid stood at 2,079mmcfd by 10am Wednesday, 171mmcfd lower than expected.
Of the current supply, 1,565mmcfd is coming from domestic gas fields and 514mmcfd from imported LNG.
Petrobangla has dismissed social media rumors claiming gas supply would be completely suspended for four days, stating that supply will not be fully cut off anywhere.
However, the state-run company warned that gas pressure could temporarily drop in some areas during the maintenance period.
Bangladesh currently operates two floating LNG terminals in Moheshkhali: one by Summit Group (500mmcfd capacity) and another by Excelerate Energy (600mmcfd capacity).
The combined capacity of these two terminals is 1,100mmcfd, and similar maintenance was previously carried out at the Summit terminal in December 2025.
